record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: The “tableau switching” process has a correspondence with jeu de taquin.[BenSottStroom1996] There is a “shifted tableau switching” process that similarly corresponds to shifted jeu de taquin. However there is an alternative “modified shifting tableau switching” process with certain better properties. “It would be very nice to develop a modified version of shifted jeu de taquin which plays the same role as that of the shifted jeu de taquin in the shifted switching process.”

evidence.quote: [ChoiNamSOh2019, sec. 1] The “tableau switching” process has a correspondence with jeu de taquin.[BenSottStroom1996] There is a “shifted tableau switching” process that similarly corresponds to shifted jeu de taquin. However there is an alternative “modified shifting tableau switching” process with certain better properties. “It would be very nice to develop a modified version of shifted jeu de taquin which plays the same role as that of the shifted jeu de taquin in the shifted switching process.”

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A shifted Young diagram of strict partition shape λ = (λ₁ > λ₂ > … > λ_ℓ > 0) is the array of cells in row i and column j with i ≤ j ≤ i + λ_i − 1. A shifted Young tableau is a filling of such a diagram with entries from a totally ordered alphabet (with possible primed letters) that is weakly increasing along rows and columns, with primed entries strictly increasing along rows and unprimed entries strictly increasing along columns.

Tableau switching (Benkart–Sottile–Stroomer) takes a pair (S,T) where S has shape μ ⊂ λ and T has skew shape λ/μ, and produces a pair (T′,S′) by repeatedly performing local "switches" that interchange adjacent boxes labeled by letters of two different alphabets according to fixed rules. For ordinary (straight) Young tableaux, the resulting bijection coincides with iterated jeu de taquin slides.

In the shifted setting, two distinct analogues of switching exist:
(i) the shifted tableau switching process, which corresponds to shifted jeu de taquin in the same way as in the unshifted case;
(ii) the modified shifted tableau switching process, which has additional desirable structural properties (involutivity and good behaviour with respect to the lattice property and shifted Littlewood–Richardson coefficients).

Problem. Define a "modified shifted jeu de taquin" procedure on shifted skew tableaux that bears the same relationship to the modified shifted tableau switching process as ordinary shifted jeu de taquin does to the shifted tableau switching process. That is, construct an explicit local sliding algorithm on shifted skew tableaux such that:
(a) iterating its slides on a shifted skew tableau T inside a pair (S,T) recovers the output of the modified shifted tableau switching applied to (S,T);
(b) it induces the same equivalence relation on shifted skew tableaux as the modified shifted switching process; and
(c) it shares the structural compatibilities (involutivity, lattice property, and the corresponding identities for Schur P/Q-functions) enjoyed by the modified shifted switching.

Prove that the proposed modified shifted jeu de taquin satisfies (a)–(c).

artifact.status_search_result: The shifted tableau switching and the modified shifted tableau switching were introduced by Choi, Nam, and Oh (J. Korean Math. Soc. 56 (2019)). While shifted jeu de taquin corresponds to the shifted switching process, no published construction of an analogous "modified" shifted jeu de taquin matching the modified switching process was found in the search results; the question is posed as an open problem and no resolution is visible in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Shifted tableau switchings and shifted Littlewood–Richardson coefficients
status_evidence.snippet: Two shifted analogues of the tableau switching process: the shifted tableau switching process and the modified shifted tableau switching process… share nice properties with the tableau switching process.
status_evidence.claim: The two shifted analogues of switching are introduced and studied, but a modified shifted jeu de taquin counterpart is not constructed.

status_evidence.title: J. Korean Math. Soc. 56 (2019), 947–984
status_evidence.snippet: The final section is devoted to the modified shifted tableau switching and its applications.
status_evidence.claim: The modified shifted switching is developed; a corresponding jeu de taquin is left as a desideratum.
